topic: Corporate Rebels 1-60 · outdated industrial management models (3/6)

passage.text: Bureaucrats still run the majority of modern workplaces. Most current organisational models have their roots in the industrial revolution and are based mainly on the ideas of Taylor and others. Their constant pursuit of efficiency pushed many organisations to achieve the highest productivity at the lowest possible cost in energy, time and money. As a result, traditional organisations successfully introduced strong hierarchies and strict rules, and made work increasingly specialised. This is why we are now accustomed to structuring our organisations like pyramids, with rigid departments separated by layers of management.

taps.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
taps.correct: Modern organisations are based on industrial-era ideas emphasising efficiency through strict hierarchies and specialisation.
wrong: Taylor invented the pyramid structure that all modern organisations now use.
Bureaucrats have recently replaced all other management systems in workplaces.
taps.explain: First option captures the main point; others misrepresent scope or causation.
